# Get-ZbxProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the proxies that collect data for the server.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxProxy [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-Id <ulong[]>] [-ProxyGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]>] [-SelectAssignedHosts] [-SelectHosts] [-SelectProxyGroup] [-SelectApm] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ByName

```
Get-ZbxProxy [-Name] <string[]> [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-ProxyGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]>] [-SelectAssignedHosts] [-SelectHosts] [-SelectProxyGroup] [-SelectApm] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### ById

```
Get-ZbxProxy [-SortField <string[]>] -Id <ulong[]> [-ProxyGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]>] [-SelectAssignedHosts] [-SelectHosts] [-SelectProxyGroup] [-SelectApm] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```


## DESCRIPTION

A proxy collects data for the server from the hosts assigned to it, so a remote site needs only one connection to the server. The Get-ZbxProxy cmdlet reads them with proxy.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole proxy.get selection in -Filter. -ProxyGroup narrows the result to the proxies of the given proxy groups, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixProxy objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a proxy by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' | Select-Object ProxyId, Name, OperatingMode, State, LastAccess
```

-Name matches the proxy's name exactly. State, Version and LastAccess are what the server last heard from it.

### Example 2: Find proxies with a wildcard

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-*' | Select-Object Name, OperatingMode, Address, Port
```

A * in -Name turns the exact match into a search.

### Example 3: List the hosts each proxy monitors

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-*' -SelectHosts |
    Select-Object Name, @{ n = 'Hosts'; e = { $_.Hosts.HostName -join ', ' } }
```

-SelectHosts adds the hosts to each proxy; they are host records (HostName is the host's technical name).

### Example 4: Count proxies without reading them

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Search @{ name = 'proxy-' } -CountOutput
```

-Search matches substrings of wire fields (here name); -CountOutput returns the number only (proxy.get's countOutput).

## INPUTS

- `ulong[]`: Bound to -Id (ByPropertyName).
- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxyGroup>[]`: Bound to -ProxyGroup (ByPropertyName). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
- `PSObject`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Each object as the API answers it.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixProxy`: The proxy read model, as returned by the Zabbix API.
